newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO says Albanian food supply threatened by unrest.
newsitem.headline: FAO says Albanian food supply threatened by unrest.

text.p: Albania requires significant imports of wheat but unrest has limited the government's already reduced ability to buy it, the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Thursday.

FAO said in a news alert that the upheavals in the Balkan country had threatened food supplies. "Outbreaks of civil unrest in Albania since early March are aggravating the already difficult food supply situation," it said.

"Recent insecurity problems are threatening the continuity of wheat and other food supplies. State warehouses have been pillaged, imports interrupted due to border closures and transportation within the country hampered by insecurity," FAO added.
The Rome-based agency said Albania was already largely reliant on imports of wheat to meet its needs for bread after a poor harvest in 1996.

"With the total wheat import gap in 1996/97 estimated to be in the region of 700,000 tonnes, significant imports of wheat are still required to ensure continuity of bread supplies to the bulk of the population until the 1997 domestic crop becomes available," the report said.
Prices of basic food such as vegetables, fruit and livestock products had also been pushed up by the unrest, the FAO said.
It added prospects for higher production from this year's harvest were not good.
"Prospects for agricultural production in 1997 are very uncertain," it said.
"Uncertainty over the 1997 cereal crop is now heightened by the recent civil unrest."
Albania has been swept by violence since January when a series of popular but fraudulent investment schemes collapsed, wiping out millions of dollars in savings.
Riots and protests against the schemes were followed by a popular uprising in the south with thousands of people seizing weapons from army depots and setting up rebel councils.
